sections.markdown:
# Accuracy and teaching notes

Stopping figures are source estimates under stated good conditions, not guarantees. Preserve the physical68 shoulder-check requirement despite physical69 language claiming mirror adjustment eliminates blind spots. The guide gives an eighteen-inch parallel-parking requirement and separately lists parking more than two feet from the curb as prohibited; retain the stricter explicit parking instruction without treating the second threshold as permission. The full narrow-street turn sequence relies on a diagram and practical maneuver instruction, which is not inferred from extraction. Current parking distances and legal exceptions remain issuer/legal review debt. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06] [A07] [A08] [A09] [A10] [A11]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Look ahead, check around, leave room; downhill toward, uphill away”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: Perception, reaction and braking are successive components of total stopping travel. An access aisle is reserved operating space beside an accessible parking bay.
Misconception to correct: Correctly adjusted mirrors remove the need to turn and check a blind spot, or the three-second basic interval is enough in every condition. The cited rules retain a shoulder check and extra space when conditions require it.
